label: Task Completion Time
aliases: time_spent; completion_duration; task_time; taskTime; completion_time; completionTime; time_to_complete_task; duration; time_on_task; response_time; reaction_time; rt; task_duration
notes: Lower-is-better; report central tendency + dispersion.

label: Task Success Rate
notes: Define success criteria clearly.

label: Error Rate
notes: Distinguish slips vs mistakes if available.

label: Efficiency
notes: Report how computed (e.g., tasks/min; actions/task).

label: Touch Offset
aliases: touch_offset_mm; touch_error_mm; tap_offset; tap_offset_mm; touch_distance_to_target; pointing_offset_mm
notes: Touch accuracy: Euclidean distance between where a touch landed and the target centre, in mm on the screen, averaged over touches. Offsets in px need the display's pixel pitch (a scale_conversions block in the study mapping). Not for one-dimensional or angular endpoint deviations along a movement axis (Fitts' effective width) or for counts of missed targets (error_rate).

label: NASA-TLX Composite Score
aliases: tlxScore; TLXScore; tlx_score; NASA_TLX_SCORE; nasa_tlx_score; nasa_tlx_total; TLX_total; raw_tlx; rtlx
notes: Derived summary score. Lower is better; report central tendency + dispersion.

label: Mental Demand
aliases: cognitive_load; mental_load; workload_rating; tlx_mental_demand; nasa_tlx_mental; NASA-TLX1; TLX1; tlx1; NASA_TLX1; nasa_tlx1; MentalLoad; ML

label: Mental Effort (Paas scale)
notes: Paas, F. G. W. C. (1992). Journal of Educational Psychology, 84(4), 429-434. Anchors: very, very low (1) to very, very high (9) mental effort.

label: Rating Scale Mental Effort (RSME)
notes: Zijlstra, F. R. H. (1993). Efficiency in work behaviour: A design approach for modern tools. PhD thesis, Delft University of Technology. Vertical 0-150 line with anchors.

label: Physical Demand
aliases: TLX2; tlx2; NASA_TLX2; nasa_tlx2; physical_demand; tlx_physical

label: Temporal Demand
aliases: TLX3; tlx3; NASA_TLX3; nasa_tlx3; temporal_demand; tlx_temporal

label: Performance (TLX)
aliases: TLX4; tlx4; NASA_TLX4; nasa_tlx4; performance; tlx_performance
notes: Note: scale direction is inverted for this subscale in raw NASA-TLX scoring.

label: Effort
aliases: TLX5; tlx5; NASA_TLX5; nasa_tlx5; effort; tlx_effort

label: Frustration
aliases: TLX6; tlx6; NASA_TLX6; nasa_tlx6; frustration; tlx_frustration

label: DALI Total Score
notes: Driving Activity Load Index (Pauzié 2008). Mean of 6 subscales, each 0–5.

label: sART Total Score
notes: Total = Understanding − (Demand − Supply). Range depends on subscale computation.

label: sART Understanding Subscale
notes: Understanding subscale of the Situation Awareness Rating Technique (SART; Taylor 1990). Scored 0–20. Distinct from eHMI comprehension items — do not pool with understanding_rating.

label: Perceived Safety
notes: Bipolar 7-point scale (−3 to +3) as used in eHMI studies.

label: Perceived Risk
notes: Visual Analogue Scale for perceived risk. In osf_cwd6h, ArduinoData1 encodes this measure.

label: Trust in Automation / eHMI
notes: Generic single-item trust. For multi-item scales, use TiA or Jian subscales.

label: TiA — Trust in Automation
notes: Overall TiA subscale. Not to be confused with the single-item trust_rating.

label: Jian Trust Scale
notes: 12-item trust/distrust checklist (Jian, Bisantz & Drury 2000). Mean of trust items on 1–7.

label: Understanding / Comprehension (eHMI)
notes: eHMI signal comprehension item. Do NOT use for sART Understanding subscale — see sart_understanding.

label: Usability (SUS Total)
aliases: sus_score; system_usability_scale; SUSScore; susScore; SYSTEM_USABILITY_SCORE; system_usability_score; SUS_total

label: UEQ — Pragmatic Quality (PQ)
notes: UEQ-S pragmatic quality = mean(perspicuity, efficiency, dependability).

label: UEQ — Hedonic Quality (HQ)
notes: UEQ-S hedonic quality = mean(stimulation, novelty).

label: van der Laan Acceptance — Usefulness Subscale
notes: Derived subscale score; mean of AOA usefulness items.

label: van der Laan Acceptance — Satisfying Subscale
notes: Derived subscale score; mean of AOA satisfying items.

label: SSQ Total Score
notes: Simulator Sickness Questionnaire total. Max theoretical = 235.62. Scores >20 indicate concern.

label: VRSQ Score
notes: VR Sickness Questionnaire. 9 items, 0–100% score.

label: IPQ — General Presence
notes: Single-item 'sense of being there' (0–6).

label: Godspeed — Perceived Safety
notes: Godspeed safety subscale. Distinct from the bipolar perceived_safety item.

label: Arousal
notes: SAM arousal manikin. High = excited/aroused, low = calm.

label: PANAS — Positive Affect
notes: Mean of 10 positive items, each 1–5.

label: PANAS — Negative Affect
notes: Mean of 10 negative items, each 1–5.

label: Usability Problems
notes: If severity is rated, include scale.

label: Standard Deviation of Lateral Position
notes: Key driving performance metric. Lower = better lane keeping.

label: Time to Collision
notes: Higher TTC = safer following distance.

label: Takeover Time
notes: Time from TOR (takeover request) to first driver input.

label: Electrodermal Activity (EDA/GSR)
aliases: gsr; skin_conductance; eda; galvanic_skin_response; SCL; SCR

label: Heart Rate Variability (RMSSD)
aliases: hrv; HRV; RMSSD; rmssd; heart_rate_variability; rr_interval; SDNN
notes: Report RMSSD or SDNN; specify which.

label: Eye-Tracking Metrics (generic)
notes: DEPRECATED — prefer fixation_duration, fixation_count, saccade_rate, dwell_time.

label: Pedestrian Crossing Time
aliases: time on intersection; time_on_intersection; crossing_time; crossing_duration
notes: Time the pedestrian spends on the intersection / crossing (eHMI-for-All crossing-event logs: time on intersection). The logs' total trial time is a different measure and is not an alias.

label: Crossing Initiation Time
notes: Latency before the pedestrian steps onto the crossing.

label: Number of Collisions
aliases: collision with cars; collision_with_cars; collisions; collision_count; number_of_collisions; num_collisions
notes: Pedestrian-vehicle collisions per trial (safety outcome).

label: Perceived User–Vehicle Conflict
notes: Subjective conflict/disagreement with the automated vehicle's decision. Composite = mean of 5 items (one reverse-scored). Lower = less conflict.

label: Perceived Conflict (item 2)
notes: Reverse-scored in the source analysis (C2_inv).

label: STS-AD Situational Trust (composite)
notes: Situational Trust Scale for Automated Driving. Composite = mean of 6 items (items 2/4/5 reverse-scored). Distinct from Körber TiA and Jian trust — do not pool with tia_* or jian_trust.

label: STS-AD trust item 2
notes: Reverse-scored in the source analysis (ST2_inv).

label: STS-AD trust item 4
notes: Reverse-scored in the source analysis (ST4_inv).

label: STS-AD trust item 5
notes: Reverse-scored in the source analysis (ST5_inv).

label: Perceived Task Feasibility
notes: Composite = mean of 2 items (one reverse-scored, A2_inv).

label: Task Feasibility (item 2)
notes: Reverse-scored in the source analysis (A2_inv).

label: Perceived Vehicle Influence on Decision
notes: How strongly the vehicle's behaviour influenced the user's decision.

label: Psychological Reactance
notes: Motivational opposition to a perceived threat to behavioural freedom (e.g. a digital-wellbeing intervention). Lower = less reactance.

label: Intervention Responsiveness (latency)
notes: Time taken to respond to an in-situ intervention (scrolling-in-the-deep: latency in seconds). Unbounded — no canonical_range.

label: Sleepiness (KSS)
notes: 1 = extremely alert, 9 = very sleepy / fighting sleep.

label: UMUX (Usability Metric for User Experience)
notes: Four 7-point items. Odd items score (response − 1), even items (7 − response); the sum / 24 × 100.

label: UMUX-Lite
notes: UMUX items 1 and 3 (7-point): (item1 + item3 − 2) / 12 × 100. Some studies report the regression-adjusted score (0.65 × raw + 22.9), which is on the SUS scale; say which one in the study mapping.

label: Single Ease Question (SEQ)
notes: Asked after each task: 1 = very difficult, 7 = very easy.

label: UES-SF – Perceived Usability
notes: The items are negatively worded; higher = better after reverse-scoring.

label: Creativity Support Index (CSI)
notes: Factor scores weighted by the paired-factor comparisons, scaled to 0–100.

label: PXI – Ease of Control
notes: Each PXI construct is the mean of three items from −3 (strongly disagree) to 3 (strongly agree).

label: PXI – Challenge
notes: Agreement that the challenge fit the player's skill (higher = better fit).

label: GEQ – Competence
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)
notes: Each GEQ component is the mean of its items from 0 (not at all) to 4 (extremely).

label: GEQ – Sensory and Imaginative Immersion
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)

label: GEQ – Flow
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)

label: GEQ – Challenge
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)

label: GEQ – Tension/Annoyance
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)

label: GEQ – Negative Affect
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)

label: GEQ – Positive Affect
instruments: GEQ core module (IJsselsteijn, de Kort & Poels 2013)

label: IMI – Interest/Enjoyment
notes: Each IMI subscale is the mean of its items from 1 (not at all true) to 7 (very true).

label: Misery Scale (MISC) motion-sickness rating
notes: 0 = no problems, 1 = some discomfort without specific symptoms, 2–5 = vague to severe symptoms without nausea, 6–9 = slight to severe nausea, 10 = vomiting. Often logged repeatedly; say in the mapping whether a column is a mean, a maximum or a single rating.

label: Presence (Slater–Usoh–Steed questionnaire)
instruments: SUS presence questionnaire (Slater, Usoh & Steed 1994; Usoh et al. 2000)
notes: Mean of the six 7-point items. The original score counts the items answered 6 or 7 (0–6); that count is not on this scale and needs its own column. Not the System Usability Scale.

label: Flow Short Scale (FKS) – Flow
notes: Mean of the 10 flow items; fluency (6 items) and absorption (4 items) are its factors.

label: Flow Short Scale – Fluency of Performance
Flow Short Scale – Absorption by Activity
Avatar Embodiment
notes: Embodiment on the questionnaire's 1–7 agreement scale. The earlier version (Gonzalez-Franco & Peck 2018) uses −3..3 and needs shifting by 4. Ad-hoc ownership or agency items belong in their own columns.

label: Text Entry Rate (WPM)
notes: (|T| − 1) / S × 60 / 5, with |T| the transcribed length and S seconds (MacKenzie 2002).

label: Keystrokes per Character (KSPC)
notes: Input stream length / transcribed length (Soukoreff & MacKenzie 2001).

label: Uncorrected Error Rate (MSD)
notes: Minimum string distance / max(|P|, |T|) × 100 (Soukoreff & MacKenzie 2003).

label: Total Error Rate (TER)
notes: (INF + IF) / (C + INF + IF) × 100, corrected and uncorrected errors (Soukoreff & MacKenzie 2003).

label: Throughput (Fitts' law, bits/s)
notes: Effective index of difficulty / movement time (ISO 9241-411; Soukoreff & MacKenzie 2004). Curved Dragging maps its nominal throughput to efficiency (schema ≤ 3.3); new mappings use this DV.
